raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will keep to the system I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That fits my land, water conditions, labor, and the local market. I do not want to spread myself across too many crops, because wheat-maize rotation is the most stable for me and I know how to manage it well. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put most fertilizer up front with a later nitrogen topdressing, irrigate at the key stages, and keep field management simple and practical. After wheat harvest, I will quickly seed summer maize with hybrid seed to secure yield, use moderate fertilizer, irrigate when the rains are not enough, and control weeds and insects in time. I will use rotary tillage for most fields because it is cheaper and faster for me than deep ploughing every season, and it matches the machinery I can arrange. My goal is steady output and lower risk, not chasing the highest possible yield.
